5.1.support: I looked for a pre-specified analysis plan for the exploratory outcomes finalized before unblinded data were available; the report cites trial registration RBR-9b7jbxm but the plan itself is not available in the article.

5.2.support: 28-day mortality has essentially one eligible measurement definition and the report presents it once in Table 4S, so selection among multiple measurements is unlikely.

5.3.support: I looked for evidence of multiple eligible analyses of the mortality comparison; no protocol or SAP is available, so intentions for analyses cannot be judged.

D1.rationale: Sequence generated electronically with stratification, allocation concealed via central randomization; baseline differences (age, PaO2/FiO2, PaCO2) appear compatible with chance in a small trial.

D2.rationale: No blinding, but patients were sedated; deviations from protocol (catheter loss, extubation, death) were clinical events consistent with usual care, and an ITT analysis included all randomized patients.

D3.rationale: Outcome data available for all randomized participants; no loss to follow-up in any group through 28 days.

D4.rationale: All-cause mortality is objectively ascertained by the same method in both groups; although assessors were unblinded, such assessment is not influenced by knowledge of allocation.

D5.rationale: No protocol or statistical analysis plan was available for the exploratory outcomes, so conformity with pre-specified analyses cannot be verified; the number and nature of analyses could not be judged (5.1 and 5.3 NI). I depart from a strictly algorithmic 'High concerns arise only from Y/PY' reading by flagging that the missing plan leaves selection uncertainty, but no evidence of selective reporting was found.

overall.rationale: Low in domains 1-4, but some concerns in Domain 5 because the analysis plan for these exploratory outcomes is unavailable, leaving unquantifiable possibility of selective reporting; no domain is at high risk of bias.

5.1.support: I looked for a pre-specified analysis plan for the exploratory outcomes finalized before unblinded data were available; the report cites trial registration RBR-9b7jbxm but the plan itself is not available in the article.

5.2.support: Ventilator-free days is a single standard definition reported once in Table 4S, so selection among multiple measurements is unlikely, though the protocol is unavailable.

5.3.support: I looked for evidence of multiple eligible analyses of ventilator-free days; no protocol or SAP is available, so analysis intentions cannot be judged.

D1.rationale: Sequence generated electronically with stratification, allocation concealed via central randomization; baseline differences appear compatible with chance in a small trial.

D2.rationale: No blinding, but patients were sedated; deviations (catheter loss, extubation, death) were clinical events consistent with usual care, and all randomized patients were analyzed.

D3.rationale: Outcome data available for all randomized participants; no loss to follow-up in any group through 28 days.

D4.rationale: Ventilator-free days depend on weaning and extubation decisions made by unblinded clinicians who knew the assigned PEEP titration method; these provider-decision outcomes could plausibly be influenced by knowledge of allocation, though no direct evidence of influence was found.

D5.rationale: No protocol or statistical analysis plan was available for the exploratory outcomes, so conformity with pre-specified analyses cannot be verified (5.1 and 5.3 NI); no direct evidence of selective reporting was found.

overall.rationale: Some concerns in Domain 4 (unblinded weaning decisions affecting ventilator-free days) and Domain 5 (no available pre-specified analysis plan); no domain at high risk of bias, but two domains with concerns lower confidence in this result.
